text_post: Congrats on the f-close. It means you must have done something right.  Now, there is little point talking about the M3 model, although some concepts may still be relevant in keeping her around. What I read is an emotionally confused woman who is afraid to get hurt, tries to be cautious and listens to her best friend's advice on dating men. Her past is holding her back.  In a way, she is right. It's not you, it's her. That does not mean you can't do anything about it. There is no point adopting a defeatist attitude and try to play the game by her own terms. if you are confident, you lay out your terms and if she chooses not to abide by them, it's her loss. What you could do instead is be honest about her, and make her change her perceptions of your blooming relationship.  She's put in her mind that it will not work. Then, she comes up with enough excuses/rationalisation why it won't. Things are bad if you think of them as being so.  I'm not going to say that she's mental, but she is using negative associations of her previous relationship on you. Eg remember the boiling water in the pan on the kitchen stove. If you get burned the first time, you will be weary of any pan on the kitchen stove, even if it's cold water. When you encounter something new, your mind make the association with a vaguely similar past event. You may call it a shit test, but you need to disrupt that negative pattern. While she's telling you that you remind her of her ex, grab her and make her look at you in the eyes, ask her if YOU are his ex. Get her to acknowledge that you are different. She knows you are different, but her poor mental association keeps getting in her way of acknowledging that... or maybe she does not know enough. Uncertainty about the future - that's one thing that everyone faces. No big deal. Solution: live life in the moment. There is nobody in the whole world who can guarantee that they will be here tomorrow. We all make plans for the future in the belief that it will materialize. But today may be your last day on earth. But ultimately, all you have is NOW. Now is when you see that hot babe staring at you from the other side of the bar. Now is when you approach her before she's swooped away by another guy. NOW is when you make love and only focus on the two of you, without worrying about everybody else in the world. NOW is when you do things on step at a time, and enjoy the moment of being somebody you want to be with. She wanted to be touched, and you responded well to it. It's not needy. It's rewarding. Women of her age like to know that they are still attractive. Since  they are of an age when society normally tells them that younger women get all the attention, she appreciates being able to feel like a woman again. How not to be "too" needy? Well, freeze out. The ability to move one step back, and let her chase you. You can adopt the frame of being the prize, coz she is worthy of being with you, not the other way around. A person who is not needy is able to walk away. It seems counter intuitive to an AFC, but if a woman is attracted to you, a feeling of loss/disconnection triggers a woman to take action to re-establish that connection. David D talks about "the gift of missing you". Not giving her everything ensures that she will be back for more. Listening to her best friend... How old is she really? Fine, she listens to her. But how do you react to that? Well, you tell her that it's ultimately her choice. And it's not her friend who is dating you. Be laid back and give the impression that if she will be the one who will miss out. I agree i think she needs to take a six month break from dating and give herself time to figure tihings out.  There is no better way to get over a car crash than to race again. That's an advice that a famous F1 racing champion once told a journalist. Why? Coz after a car crash, your mind starts to run into "cautious" mode. The F1 driver talks about "fear of crashing again" and the best way to overcome it is to get behind the wheel as soon as possible. When you start to drive again, you realise that the last crash was an accident, you get back the joy of driving while not giving fear a chance to creep back. Similarly, the longer you take to resume dating, the more you get used to not being with somebody and the harder it becomes. Yeah, there is a lot of talk out there that "time heals". No doubt there is some element of truth in that saying, but there is also another saying that goes "love waits for noone". Life is so short and flies so fast. Why wait 6 months when you can start NOW. MM usually recommends sarging other women at the same time. If you make her aware [indirectly] that you have options, and that if she does not have a similar level of interest [or willingness to invest] in the relationship, then it will not work out anyway. If she can't accept you for who you are, then she's not worth you. Just don't give her the opportunity to play mind games with you. Dont buy into her frame that she needs to figure things out. But, I agree she has emotional baggage. But what do you do with emotional baggage? You can leave it behind. There is no law/rule that states that you have to carry it around all your life. Dont be the little puppy who will be waiting patiently at her door until she makes her mind.  Life is too short for both of you to delay things for 6 months. South Korea and Iran would have already destroyed the whole world by then[a bit exaggerated but you get the point].

text_post: I agree with this... Most women, most people, tend to be attracted to that which they associate with internally.  (that's confusing... here...)
